newsitem.title: GERMANY: German malting barley quality suffered in May.
newsitem.headline: German malting barley quality suffered in May.

text.p: Insufficient rain in May weighed on likely harvest quality and volumes in German spring barley regions looking to market their crop as malting barley, specialist broker Jochen Mautner GmbH said.
German spring barley plantings this year are down two percent from last year's at 780,000 hectares, he said.

Mautner, who publishes a bi-monthly survey of acreages, varieties and crop progress in 12 German states, said yields should be lower than expected and protein levels high. Protein content must be low to qualify barley for malting purposes.

Protein levels would be high in parts of Bavaria, Baden-Wuerttemberg, Rhineland-Palatinate, Saxony, Schleswig-Holstein and Thuringia, as a result of cold and dry conditions earlier this year, which thinned crops and delayed nitrogen absorbtion.
In the other six German states surveyed, spring barley crops benefitted from sufficient rain and were "medium to good," with minimum pest levels.
Mautner's analysis excluded the city states of Hamburg, Bremen and Berlin as well as the Saarland.
Malting barley and malt markets were quiet and prices weak for the time being, Mautner noted, adding the brewing industry was well covered.

Farm price and marketing office ZMP listed ex-wholesalers prices at 270-285 marks a tonne. It noted the 1997 crop should be historically high and growers were looking for export opportunities, for example to southern Europe, more affected by dry conditions than Germany.
In 1996, some 57 percent of the German spring barley crop of 4.18 million tonnes qualified as malting barley, according to Mautner.
